items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: he had Obey Bearcat Walker and a couple of more fighters.

ctx.x: And I had a little -- little tricks in the tap dancing that I knew, and people enjoyed it, so I would make quite a bit of money, which I'd take back to my mother's mother, and I'd tell her what had happened during the day, and she would always tell me where to go the next day -- and the next time, you know, to go somewhere's else, you know. And she said it was a nice thing I was doing; it was healthy and so forth, and that I may grow up to be a famous tap dancer like Florence Mills or someone, you see.

So I continued to do this. In the meantime I got back to the 81 Theater, to this lady's record shop, Miss Lucille Achet. That was George Roby's daughter-in-law. And he was a fight promoter, and he had Obey Bearcat Walker and a couple of more fighters. Obey was a heavyweight, and the others was -- there was a bantamweight and a welterweight, you know, and he was going to bring them up to New York somewhere, what they called up North.

Now, one of the fighters didn't want to leave the South. So he stayed back. Now, as I -- I was out in front of this lady's record shop, you know, and she had a sound system that -- and she'd play music from inside the shop, and it would come out back over the sidewalk as the people walking along, you know, attract their attentions.
